issues.detail: The Greek text uses 'τι δε βλεπεις' (why do you see) and 'ου κατανοεις' (you do not perceive/notice), but the Vietnamese translation adds 'chẳng xem xét' (do not examine/consider). While similar, 'κατανοεις' implies a failure to perceive or understand what is there, whereas 'xem xét' implies a failure to deliberate or investigate. More importantly, the Greek 'τι δε βλεπεις' is a rhetorical question structure; the Vietnamese 'Sao ngươi thấy' captures the 'why', but the switch from 'see' (βλέπω) to 'examine' (xem xét) for the second verb changes the nature of the action.
